h: Holy Work Throughout the Week Prepares the Shabbos

p: וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת וְגוֹ׳ (וַיִּקְרָא כג, ג)
and on the seventh day a Shabbos, etc." (Vayikra 23:3).
In every place where Shabbos is mentioned,
the six workdays are mentioned first,
that is, the Shabbosos of Hashem.
And this is as we said:
that according to the holiness of the workdays,
so is the holiness of Shabbos.
and the seventh day is a Shabbos, etc."
That is: in the First Tablets
"A place in which there is no forgetting, etc."
just as I rested on it"
"For in six days He made, etc.,
and He rested on the seventh day;
that is, "And you shall walk in His ways."
And this is what they said in the Mechilta (Bachodesh 7):
just as with the Shabbos of Hashem Yisbarach,
and afterward the repose on Shabbos.
That is why it is written,
directed for the sake of Heaven.
For since at the utterance "I am"
Torah study was implanted in their heart,
and at the utterance "You shall have no"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their heart
(as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah
it is likewise written in this language,
as they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 69b):
like the creation of the world,
and one master holds like Adam HaRishon."
"You shall labor and do all your work":
that all the work of this world should be
in holiness, directed for the sake of Heaven;
through the "Keep" that is after it.
And in parashas Mishpatim it is written (Shemos 23:12),
"Six days you shall do your deeds,
and on the seventh day you shall rest."
There it speaks of the Shemittah year,
when they are free all year
so that for this reason one might have thought
that Shabbos would not be needed at all;
that Shemittah does not uproot the Shabbos of Creation from its place
who are likened to Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim
in which they merit extra holiness.
That is why it says beforehand,
"Six days you shall do your deeds"
that is, deeds that are permitted,
and then everything is in holiness.
And in parashas Ki Sisa and parashas Vayakhel,
דִּכְתִיב שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים יֵעָשֶׂה מְלָאכָה (שְׁמוֹת לא, טו)
where it is written "Six days work shall be done" (Shemos 31:15),
וְכֵן שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּעָשֶׂה מְלָאכָה (שָׁם לה, ב)
and likewise "Six days work shall be done" (Shemos 35:2)
there they were commanded regarding the work of the Mishkan,
and all the activity of the workdays was
the work of the Mishkan, in holiness;
and "shall be done" is written in the passive,
according to what they said in the Midrash
"'And the House, when it was built'
and so it is written in the holy Zohar
regarding the work of the Mishkan,
'And all the work was completed, etc.'"
But here, why is it written
when it speaks for all generations?
to what is said after this:
"It is a Shabbos to Hashem in all your dwellings."
regarding Shabbos, why do I need it?
since it is written in the section of the festivals,
it should require sanctification like the festivals."
And according to what is written in Rashi's commentary
since it does not depend on the month?
אַךְ דְּרָשָׁה זוֹ אִיתָא גַּם כֵּן
But this derivation is also found
does not require sanctification by Beis Din."
that the sanctification of the festivals
הוּא מַה שֶּׁרֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין אוֹמֵר
is what the head of the Beis Din says
and he derives it from what is written,
And the meaning is as we have said many times:
that for this reason it is called Rosh Chodesh,
because it is the head of the month,
and in it is included all the holiness
that will be in this month,
That is why it is written "callings of holiness":
for the head of the Beis Din says
and through this the holiness is called
to the festival that will be in this month.
that every Rosh Chodesh must be sanctified,
even in a month that has no festival;
דְּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ אִיקְרֵי מוֹעֵד
for in truth Rosh Chodesh too is called a festival
though in the Torah we do not find it,
and it is learned from the Kesuvim;
for the months that have festivals.
דְּגַם שַׁבָּת תִּיבְעֵי קִידּוּשׁ בֵּית דִּין
that Shabbos too requires sanctification by Beis Din:
that the head of the Beis Din would need
to sanctify the first day of the week,
so that its seventh would be Shabbos.
And this is what one might have thought
because regarding Shabbos too it is written,
"a day of rest, a calling of holiness."
וְזֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן כַּוָּונַת רַשִׁ״י
And this too was Rashi's intent,
only he was brief, as is his way.
And about this the pasuk comes to exclude,
"It is a Shabbos to Hashem in all your dwellings":
even in a place where there is no Beis Din,
it is a Shabbos to Hashem,
which was sanctified in the six days of Creation.
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם עַל כָּל פָּנִים
must sanctify it from the first day of the week,
for it is written of it, "a calling of holiness."
that is, that the deeds of the workdays
of the Holy One, blessed is He
For it first cites, regarding the deeds of tzaddikim,
"The Sanctuary, Hashem, that Your hands established";
since it refers to the Mikdash,
which was made by Hashem Yisbarach,
as it says, "And the House, when it was built,"
וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו מַגִּיד הָרָקִיעַ (תְּהִלִּים יט, ב)
"And the firmament tells of His handiwork" (Tehillim 19:2)
And nevertheless it is called His handiwork.
But it is as we have said many times:
"In your mouth and in your heart, to do it,"
and it does not say "in your deeds";
this is because a person's main effort is
"in your mouth and in your heart,"
but the completion of the deed
that is why it is written "to do it."
And as is written in the holy Zohar
"What does Hashem your God ask of you
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שְׁלַח, חֵלֶק ג קס, א)
and in the holy Zohar (Shelach, III 160a):
but the completion of the deed
And this is what it says,
that is, that it should be
whose purpose is for the sake of Heaven:
and to raise his children to Torah study,
for then everything becomes an act of mitzvah,
as the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote
And this is called the handiwork
of the Holy One, blessed is He,
And through this you will merit
to call the holiness to Shabbos,
according to the preparation on one's part
And this is "It is a Shabbos to Hashem
from the first day of the week, "toward your Shabbos."

paragraphs.text: Source: Kesubos 5a — “מיתיבי: ״השמים מספרים כבוד אל ומעשה ידיו מגיד הרקיע״! הכי קאמר: מעשה ידיהם של צדיקים מי מגיד — הרקיע, ומאי ניהו — מטר.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 20) — “The Gemara raises an objection: “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands” (Psalms 19:2).
